svg.title: Improved hierarchical financial AI architecture with signal store, event bus, and feedback loop
svg.desc: Five-stage architecture: sources feed Layer 1 LLM extraction, results land in a versioned Signal Store, Layer 2 deterministically composes themes, Layer 3 LLM synthesizes verdicts, and a feedback loop calibrates weights from realized returns. An event bus drives selective invalidation.
svg.text: LLMs at the edges (L1 interprets, L3 writes); deterministic math in the middle
Filings, decks, prowess feeds, news webhooks — each emits a typed event

g.text: Event bus — typed events with source_hash, timestamp, severity
{source: AR_FY26, company: TATAMOTORS, type: filing, hash: sha256, urgency: routine}

svg.text: Triggered only when source_hash changes • idempotent • cost: ~$0.60 per source

g.text: Per source: parse → chunk → extract signals → assign w, b → tag with prompt_version
{metric, t, value, w, b, source, confidence}

svg.text: Versioned, queryable, immutable-by-default • the single source of truth
Themes are config, not code • new themes don't require re-extraction • cost: ~$0 per theme
Only LLM call on user query • prose, not numbers • cost: ~$0.045 per verdict

g.text: cites N₁, N₂, M₂ by id

svg.text: Realized returns at 1Q/1Y/3Y horizons calibrate weights and impact bias
L1 amortised: ~$1.6M/yr • Signal Store: ~$2K/yr storage • L2 themes: ~$0/query
Iteration cost (tweak weights): $0.045 vs $1,800 in monolithic = 40,000× cheaper
Net: LLM spend becomes a fixed annual cost, not a per-query tax
System self-improves as feedback accumulates — unlike the monolith
